title: "Quiz 3"
author: "Mohamud Said"
date: "2025-10-30"
output: html_document
---
1. Load the spotify dataset (available in github repository).
```{r}
library(readr)
library(ggplot2)
spotifyDat <- read_csv("spotifyDat Fall26.csv")
View(spotifyDat)
```

2. Create a bar graph of the artist column (Hint: use theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90)) to rotate the x axis).
```{r}


ggplot(spotifyDat, aes(x = artist)) + geom_bar() + theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90))
```

3. Add genre as a third variable in your graph.
```{r}
ggplot(spotifyDat, aes(x = artist, color= genre)) + geom_bar() + theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90))

```

4. Use color brewer to add color to your graph in 3. 
```{r}
library(RColorBrewer)
ggplot(spotifyDat, aes(x = artist, fill= genre)) + geom_bar() + theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90)) + scale_fill_brewer(palette= "Set3")

# There isn't a large enough palette! 
```

5. Place the legend for the graph you made in 3 on the bottom of the graph. 
```{r}
ggplot(spotifyDat, aes(x = artist, fill= genre)) + geom_bar() + theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90), legend.position="bottom") + scale_fill_brewer(palette= "Set3") 
```

As you probably recognized, the graph you made is really hard to read.

6. Separate the genre column into multiple columns (e.g. so each genre listed is in a unique column)
```{r}
library(tidyr)
library(dplyr)
spotifyDat <- mutate(spotifyDat, genre = na_if(genre,"set()")) #had to go back and do this one, lmao.
spotifyDatSep <- separate(spotifyDat, genre, into = c("genre1", "genre2", "genre3", "genre4"), sep = ",")
```

7. Use these genre columns to create a dataset in long format. 
```{r}
spotifyDatLong <- pivot_longer(spotifyDatSep, cols = c("genre1","genre2","genre3","genre4"), names_to="genreNum", values_to="genre", values_drop_na = TRUE)
```

8.use facet wrap to make graphs of artist by genre 
```{r}
ggplot(spotifyDatLong, aes(y= artist, fill= genre)) + geom_bar() + theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90), legend.position="none") + facet_wrap(~genre, scales="free_y") 

#HOLY COW THATS AN UGLY GRAPH!!!! 
```

9. Create a graph that includes the variables tempo and dancability. 
```{r}
ggplot(spotifyDatLong, aes(tempo, danceability)) + geom_point() 
```

10. Add popularity as a third variable. 
```{r}
ggplot(spotifyDatLong, aes(tempo, danceability, color=popularity)) + geom_point() 

```

11. Use viridis as a color in your graph from #10
```{r}
library(viridis)
ggplot(spotifyDatLong, aes(tempo, danceability, color=popularity)) + geom_point() + scale_color_viridis( option="magma")
```
